blogs.title: Direct Preference Optimization, Explained: Aligning AI Without Reinforcement Learning
blogs.description: A plain‑English tour of DPO and why it matters. We break down how today’s RLHF pipeline trains a reward model and then uses PPO, and how DPO replaces that complexity with a simple preference‑classification loss that directly nudges the model toward human‑preferred answers—no on‑policy sampling or fragile RL loops required.

blogs.title: From RLHF to DPO: The Alignment Pipeline, Simplified
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step look at the end‑to‑end workflow. Starting from an instruction‑tuned reference model, we show how to collect preference pairs, plug them into DPO, and use a single hyperparameter (beta) to control how far the model drifts from the reference. We highlight the engineering wins: stability, fewer knobs, and lower compute.

blogs.title: How It Works: Turning Policies Into Rewards (and Back Again)
blogs.description: An intuitive dive under the hood. We explain how DPO uses a classic preference model (Bradley–Terry) and a change of variables so the language model itself implicitly defines a reward. The key idea: compare log‑probabilities of preferred vs dispreferred responses relative to a reference model, and weight updates by how “wrong” the model is.

blogs.title: DIY DPO: A Practical Guide to Training With Human Preferences
blogs.description: An implementer’s checklist. Learn how to format preference data, freeze a reference model, compute log‑probabilities for two candidate responses, and train with a binary cross‑entropy loss. We cover choosing beta, reusing public datasets when the original SFT model isn’t available, avoiding degeneration, and evaluating with win rates.

blogs.title: Do Results Match the Hype? DPO vs PPO on Sentiment, Summaries, and Chat
blogs.description: A tour of the paper’s benchmarks. See how DPO outperforms PPO on the reward–KL frontier for sentiment control (even when PPO uses ground‑truth rewards), matches or beats PPO on Reddit TL;DR summarization, improves single‑turn dialogue without heavy compute, and generalizes better than PPO to news summarization in out‑of‑distribution tests.

blogs.title: Theory Corner: Your Language Model Is Secretly a Reward Model
blogs.description: Why DPO is more than a hack. We outline the reward equivalence classes in Bradley–Terry/Plackett–Luce models, show that DPO loses no expressivity by reparameterizing rewards via the policy and reference model, and explain how this avoids the variance and baseline pitfalls that make actor‑critic RL unstable.

blogs.title: Better Preference Data, Better Models: Collecting and Evaluating Preferences
blogs.description: Practical advice on building and reusing preference datasets. We explain sampling candidate answers from a reference model, labeling pairs, and validating progress with win rates. We also summarize the paper’s finding that GPT‑4 judgments correlate well with humans, and discuss prompt sensitivity and how to run human checks responsibly.

blogs.title: Limits and Next Steps: Where DPO Shines—and What’s Next
blogs.description: A candid look at trade‑offs. We cover open questions like out‑of‑distribution robustness, reward over‑optimization, scaling to frontier models, and choosing beta. We also map opportunities: self‑labeling with DPO, multimodal generative models, and when you might still prefer PPO or Best‑of‑N strategies.
